## What this graph is

The unified kernel — the PZG–BEDC tower formalized in `papers/unified_theory/lean4/UnifiedTheory/` — is **82 Lean modules** built on mathlib. Every module `import`s the modules it depends on, and `lake` topologically orders that graph to compile. So a dependency DAG already exists: it lives in the `import` lines, and the compiler walks it on every build. What has been missing is a *reading* of it — a picture that says, at a glance, where the checked core sits, where the RH-homing frontier sits, and which open leaves actually block which downstream claims.

This page renders that DAG directly from the import lines. Nothing here is hand-asserted about status; the edges are exactly the internal imports (`82` modules, `71` internal edges), and the leaf classification tracks the [full-tower gap map](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/newmath/blob/dev/papers/unified_theory/formalization/full_tower_gap_map.md). It is regenerable from source in one pass (see [Provenance](#provenance)).

## The tower spine

Grouping the 82 modules by layer gives a clean partial order. Arrows point from a layer to what it depends on. The base is `Foundation` (mark / history / rewriting) and `Arithmetic` (prime axes); the top is `Kernel` (the total object) and — carrying every open leaf of the whole tower — `Zeta`, the RH-homing layer.

```{mermaid}
graph TD
  classDef solid fill:#d7f0d7,stroke:#2f7d2f,color:#123;
  classDef frontier fill:#fdeecb,stroke:#c8891f,color:#123;

  Zeta["Zeta &middot; RH homing<br/>(12 modules &middot; all open leaves live here)"]:::frontier
  Kernel["Kernel &middot; total object<br/>(4)"]:::solid
  SelfCode["SelfCode &middot; self-coding<br/>(9)"]:::solid
  Golden["Golden &middot; golden / Beatty<br/>(27)"]:::solid
  Dynamics["Dynamics &middot; phase / cost<br/>(7)"]:::solid
  PZG["PZG &middot; carry carrier<br/>(8)"]:::solid
  Arithmetic["Arithmetic &middot; prime axes<br/>(9)"]:::solid
  Foundation["Foundation &middot; mark / history / rewriting<br/>(3)"]:::solid

  Zeta --> Golden
  Zeta --> Dynamics
  Zeta --> Arithmetic
  Kernel --> Golden
  Kernel --> PZG
  Kernel --> Arithmetic
  Kernel --> Foundation
  SelfCode --> Golden
  Golden --> PZG
  Golden --> Arithmetic
  Dynamics --> Arithmetic
  Dynamics --> Foundation
  PZG --> Arithmetic
  PZG --> Foundation
```

`Golden` is the heaviest layer (27 modules): golden-integer arithmetic, Beatty / Zeckendorf reading, the deficit and carry theory, the golden-weight arithmetic functions. It sits mid-tower — above `PZG` and `Arithmetic`, and everything self-referential (`SelfCode`) or spectral (`Zeta`) is built on top of it.

## The frontier is a fan, not a chain

The single most useful thing the DAG shows — invisible in a flat status table — is the **internal shape of the `Zeta` layer**. Of the 12 modules in the RH-homing layer, there are only **3 internal edges** between them:

- `WeilArchimedean → WeilExplicit`
- `WeilPrimeSideZeta → WeilExplicit`
- `ZeroFreeLine → RHBridge`

Everything else — the heart-electrode window analysis, the Möbius and `1/ζ` facts, the golden↔Weil bridge, the chamber count, the completed-zeta and Euler-product wrappers — are **independent leaves**, each importing mathlib directly and none importing the others. The frontier is a **fan of independent bricks**, not a dependency chain.

That is why the layer can be advanced brick by brick in parallel: there is almost no internal coupling to serialize against. And it relocates the real closure question. The tower does not converge at some internal Zeta join; it converges at the *open leaf inside each brick* — the analytic positivity, the missing oscillation theorem, the ledger that is honestly a restatement rather than a proof.

```{mermaid}
graph TD
  classDef solid fill:#d7f0d7,stroke:#2f7d2f,color:#123;
  classDef open fill:#f6d0d0,stroke:#b33,color:#123;

  WeilExplicit["WeilExplicit"]:::solid
  WeilArchimedean["WeilArchimedean<br/>(holds O-6 positivity open leaf)"]:::open
  WeilPrimeSideZeta["WeilPrimeSideZeta"]:::solid
  RHBridge["RHBridge<br/>(RH ledger &middot; restatement, not a proof)"]:::open
  ZeroFreeLine["ZeroFreeLine"]:::solid

  HeartMellin["HeartMellin<br/>(F-1 decay, sinh no-miss)"]:::solid
  HeartMobius["HeartMobius"]:::solid
  HeartOneOverZeta["HeartOneOverZeta<br/>(F-2, 1/&zeta; zero)"]:::solid
  WeilGoldenBridge["WeilGoldenBridge"]:::solid
  WeilChamberCount["WeilChamberCount"]:::solid
  Completed["Completed"]:::solid
  EulerProduct["EulerProduct"]:::solid

  WeilArchimedean --> WeilExplicit
  WeilPrimeSideZeta --> WeilExplicit
  ZeroFreeLine --> RHBridge
```

Green modules compile `0-sorryAx` (only `propext` / `Classical.choice` / `Quot.sound`, i.e. plain mathlib). The two red modules are honest about what they are: `WeilArchimedean` *registers* the O-6 archimedean positivity as an open `Prop` rather than proving it, and `RHBridge` is a faithful re-encoding of "no off-line zeros" — a ledger, never a proof.

## Where the open leaves actually sit

Because the frontier is a fan, "what is left to close" is not one monolith but a short list of named leaves, each inside one brick:

| Open leaf | Lives in | What it blocks | Why it is open |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-6 archimedean positivity | `WeilArchimedean` | closing the finite-packet Weil positivity | analytic positivity, month-scale |
| Landau Ω-oscillation theorem | *(absent from mathlib)* | the Delange → H.8 lower-bound chain | mathlib has no oscillation/Ω theorem |
| char-group Pontryagin duality | *(not yet built)* | prime-axis ↔ $\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}$ duality | needs the profinite $\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}$ |
| RH ledger | `RHBridge` | — | a faithful restatement; equivalent to RH, so never a self-standing proof |

No leaf is faked with `True.intro` or hidden behind a statement-only stub. The checked content is genuinely checked; the open content is genuinely open and named where it lives.

## Provenance {#provenance}

Both graphs are derived from the repository, not maintained by hand. The single source of truth is the set of `import UnifiedTheory.*` lines under `papers/unified_theory/lean4/UnifiedTheory/`. To regenerate the edge list and the layer counts:

```bash
cd papers/unified_theory/lean4
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, re, collections
root = "UnifiedTheory"
edges = collections.defaultdict(set); mods = set()
for dp, _, fs in os.walk(root):
    for f in fs:
        if not f.endswith(".lean"): continue
        m = os.path.join(dp, f)[:-5].replace("/", ".")
        if m == "UnifiedTheory.All": continue
        mods.add(m)
        for line in open(os.path.join(dp, f)):
            g = re.match(r"\s*import\s+(UnifiedTheory\.[\w.]+)", line)
            if g: edges[m].add(g.group(1))
for m in edges: edges[m] &= mods
layer = lambda m: m.split(".")[1] if len(m.split(".")) > 2 else "root"
le = collections.defaultdict(set)
for s, ts in edges.items():
    for t in ts:
        if layer(s) != layer(t): le[layer(s)].add(layer(t))
print(f"{len(mods)} modules, {sum(len(v) for v in edges.values())} internal edges")
for s in sorted(le):
    for t in sorted(le[s]): print(f"  {s} -> {t}")
PY
```

Counts on this page (`82` modules, `71` internal edges, `3` internal `Zeta` edges) are the output of that pass; rerun it against any commit to get the current figures.
